applicant_utility.summary: A monthly stipend of ¥48,000 at undergraduate or graduate level, or ¥30,000 at a Japanese language institute, for privately-financed international students already enrolled in Japan and facing financial difficulty, paid for 12 months from April or 6 months from October. You never apply to JASSO directly: your institution recommends you, and the number of recommendations it can make depends on how many international students it has, so the award can disappear before you ever compete. The practical filters are the income and allowance tests - other allowances excluding tuition must average under ¥90,000 a month and a Japan-based supporter's income must be under ¥5 million a year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Already-enrolled self-financed international students in Japan with strong grades, a residence status of Student, and a family or income situation that clears both the ¥90,000 monthly allowance ceiling and the ¥5 million supporter income ceiling.
application_readiness_checklist: Find out early whether your institution actually recommends applicants for this scholarship, since some do not
Ask the international students' office about your institution's allocation, because the quota depends on the number of international students enrolled
Total every allowance you receive outside tuition and check it averages under ¥90,000 a month
If you have a financial supporter in Japan, confirm their annual income is under ¥5 million yen
Confirm you hold the residence status of Student and are not a MEXT or foreign government scholarship holder
Confirm you are not simultaneously receiving JASSO Student Exchange Support Program support, which is an explicit incompatibility
common_rejection_risks: Attending an institution that does not recommend applicants, which means no route at all
Your institution's quota being exhausted before your turn
Total monthly allowances excluding tuition exceeding ¥90,000 on average
A Japan-based financial supporter earning ¥5 million or more a year
Holding a Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) or foreign government scholarship, which changes your category entirely
Receiving support under the JASSO Student Exchange Support Program, which is barred
Holding another scholarship that the rules exclude from combination with the Honors Scholarships
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and enrolment fees, which are expressly outside the allowance covered by the stipend, plus flights and any relocation costs.
document_audit: The grading criteria are set in the application guidelines issued by the institution rather than by JASSO
You must sign on the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office, so the award carries a monthly administrative obligation
You must agree to cooperate with the career path survey JASSO conducts through the institution
alerts: The scholarship is awarded for 12 months from April or 6 months from October, so a mid-year award is by design the shorter period
The language requirement does not apply to candidates at preparatory Japanese language programs, university preparatory courses or Japanese language institutes
JASSO publishes annual selection results, but the 2026 results are Japanese-language only
JASSO confirms that no university or Japanese language institute is currently suspended from recommending applicants
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Ask the international students' office at your institution about its recommendation quota and internal deadline, let the institution submit the recommendation to JASSO, then once awarded sign the designated JASSO sheet monthly at the international students' office.

official.deadline_note: There is no fixed application deadline set by JASSO. Applications for the scholarship will be accepted only from the Japanese school, and students must start the study-in-Japan program at Japanese schools during each school's designated period. The selection method of scholarship recipients differs from each school and each program.
official.application_cycle: Continuous but school-driven; awards run for study in Japan of between 8 days and one year
official.status_note: JASSO publishes the Student Exchange Support Program as an active scheme for qualified international students studying in Japan for between 8 days and one year under a student exchange agreement.
benefits: Funding for a study-in-Japan period of between 8 days and one year
eligibility: Students from all countries that have diplomatic relations with Japan; students from Taiwan and Palestine are acceptable
Students accepted by a Japanese school under a student exchange agreement or other student exchange arrangement with their home school
Students not having the financial means to study in Japan
Students eligible for a Student Visa; for study in Japan for 90 days or less, the Japanese school will arrange the status of residence
Students who, upon termination of the period of study in Japan, will complete their studies at their home school
Students demonstrating excellent academic and personal records at their home school
Students receiving more than 80,000 yen per month in total from other scholarships for study in Japan are ineligible
requirements: The study-in-Japan period must be for a short-term basis from 8 days to one year under a student exchange agreement or other student exchange arrangement between the Japanese school and the home higher educational institution outside Japan
Students must start the study-in-Japan program at Japanese schools during each school's designated period
Students must be eligible for a Student Visa, or for study of 90 days or less accept the status of residence arranged by the Japanese school
Total scholarship funding received from other scholarships for study in Japan must not exceed 80,000 yen per month
documents: The documents required by the Japanese school through which the application is submitted
selection_criteria: JASSO screens the application documents submitted by the Japanese school and decides the programs to support
The selection method of scholarship recipients is different from each school and each program

official.application_route: Apply through your home institution and the Japanese host school; JASSO accepts applications only from the Japanese school.

official.duration: Short-term study in Japan from 8 days to one year
official.description: JASSO offers a scholarship for qualified international students who are accepted by a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology or professional training college under a student exchange agreement or other student exchange arrangement on a short-term basis from 8 days to one year between the Japanese school and their home higher educational institution outside Japan.
official.program_type: Government-funded monthly stipend for exchange students on study-in-Japan programmes

applicant_utility.summary: A monthly stipend of ¥80,000 for students who come to a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology or professional training college for between 8 days and one year under an exchange agreement with their home institution. You apply through your home institution and the Japanese host school, never directly to JASSO, and JASSO screens whole programs rather than individuals - it decides which programmes to support and, separately, each school decides its own recipients. The scheme is need-based in one direction only: you must lack the financial means to study in Japan at your own expense, and total monthly funding from all other scholarships for study in Japan must not exceed ¥80,000.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students enrolled at a foreign institution with an active exchange agreement or arrangement with a Japanese school, who cannot fund a Japanese semester themselves and can return to complete their studies at home afterwards.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your home institution has an exchange agreement or arrangement with a specific Japanese school, since the scholarship is granted through that arrangement
Check with the Japanese school whether its designated intake period matches your intended start date, since students must start during each school's designated period
Total every other scholarship you receive for study in Japan and check the combined monthly figure stays at or below ¥80,000
Confirm you are eligible for a Student Visa, or that your stay is 90 days or less so the Japanese school can arrange the status of residence
Confirm with your home school that you will return to complete your degree after the Japanese period, which is an explicit condition
common_rejection_risks: Having no exchange agreement between your home institution and a Japanese school, which removes the route entirely
Total monthly scholarship funding from other Japanese scholarships exceeding ¥80,000, which is an absolute bar
Being able to fund the period yourself, since lacking the financial means to study in Japan is an eligibility condition
Not starting during the Japanese school's designated intake period
Planning to transfer into study in Japan rather than returning to your home institution
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights, accommodation and registration costs at the Japanese school, and any living costs beyond the ¥80,000 monthly stipend.
document_audit: The document set is defined by the Japanese school, since only school-submitted applications are accepted
The selection method differs from school to school and programme to programme, so ask your Japanese host school rather than JASSO
Note that receiving the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship also excludes you, since holders must not be receiving support under this programme
alerts: JASSO decides which programmes to support, not which individuals receive the stipend - the school decides that
The scheme covers stays as short as 8 days, so a summer or intensive programme can qualify
For stays of 90 days or less the Japanese school arranges the status of residence, which removes the need for a Student Visa
The programme page is dated as of 31 January 2024, so confirm current terms with the Japanese school
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Ask your home institution's international office about its Japanese exchange partners, apply to the Japanese school for the exchange place, have the Japanese school submit the scholarship application to JASSO, then start within that school's designated intake period.
